The fact that the deceased was riding on   motorcycle along with the driver and another, may not,
 itself, without anything more, make him guilty of  Contributory Negligence.
At the most it would make him  guilty of being a party to the violation of the law.
S https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  3/6  128 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, imposes a restri  on the driver of a two-wheeled motorcycle, not to carr  more than one person on the motorcycle.
Section 194-C  inserted by the Amendment Act 32 of 2019, prescribes a  penalty for violation of safety measures for Motorcycl  Drivers and Pillion Riders.
Therefore, the fact that a  person was a pillion rider on a motorcycle along with   driver and one more person on the pillion, may be a  violation of the law.

But such violation by itself, wi  anything more, cannot lead to a finding of contributor  negligence, unless it is established that his very act  riding along with two others, contributed either to th  accident or to the impact of the accident upon the vic
There must either be a causal connection between the  violation and the accident or a causal connection betw  the violation and the impact of hte accident upon the  victim.
It may so happen at times, that the accident c  have been averted or the injuries sustained could have  been of a lesser degree, if there had been no violatio  the law by the victim.
What could otherwise have resul  in a simple injury, might have resulted in a grievous   or even death due to the violation of the law by the v

It is in such cases, where, but for the violation of t  either the accident could have been averted or the imp  could have been minimized, that the principle of  contributory negligence could be invoked.
In the above circumstances, the finding of the Tribun  regarding Contributory negligence is not sustainable.

 liable to be set aside.
